action.short_description: Removing a proposed voice-assessment drug-testing pilot
action.compact_description: The agreed amendment deletes an optional automated voice-assessment pilot, including conditional testing/privacy/punitive-use elements and report/sunset clocks measured from establishment. It does not end all military drug testing or establish technology accuracy. Whole technology-versus-personnel membership remains unaccepted.
action.meaning:
The House agreed to exact PartA4to H.R.8800, offered by the designated Member, striking proposed section518of the governing RCP119–33. That chamber amendment does not itself enact the whole defense package or stop an existing operating program. The exact target is the optional voice-based risk-assessment drug-testing pilot, not all Department of Defense drug testing.
Proposed518would permit, rather than require, the Secretary to establish a pilot evaluating automated voice-based risk assessment for targeted testing of ArmedForces members in place of universal urinalysis. IF the pilot were carried out, its elements would be mandatory: use the automated technology within the DrugDemandReductionProgram, align with deterrence/security/fitness/readiness/order/discipline goals, allow results to be used for punitive or other appropriate actions, AND protect individual privacy and comply with applicable law and Department policy. Evaluation language is not evidence that the technology detects drug use accurately or improves readiness, and privacy language is not proof of actual safeguards implementation.
The conditional report would be due one year AFTER ESTABLISHMENT of the pilot, assessing testing volume, cost savings, personnel time and readiness; the conditional pilot would terminate three years AFTER ESTABLISHMENT. Those clocks are not from enactment and apply only if the optional pilot is carried out. Striking518removes this proposed authorization/elements/report/sunset together. It neither prohibits every voice technology nor establishes that an existing pilot, general testing authority, privacy law or disciplinary baseline is repealed. Current program rules, actual testing practice, validated technology performance and individual disciplinary outcomes remain uninspected.
An Aye supports deleting this proposed optional pilot; a No opposes that deletion, not necessarily every testing policy or a component-specific position about punitive use. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on this exact automated assessment/testing-technology authorization and its removal. A competing boundary treats the whole choice as military personnel/health oversight. Independent baseline, exact-version and taxonomy review is required. No deployed surveillance, proven accuracy, privacy harm, savings, readiness improvement, motive or enactment is inferred.
limitations: Exact deletion of proposed518, not repeal of all militarydrugtesting or an operatingpilot.
Pilot MAY; elements/report/sunset conditional if carriedout, including punitive-use and privacy/compliance requirements.
One-year report and three-year termination from ESTABLISHMENT, not enactment.
No validated accuracy, deployment, actualprivacyprotection/harm, savings or individualdisciplinary outcome certified.
Whole automatedassessment technology versus militarypersonnel/health taxonomy remains unaccepted.

action.short_description: Studying Federal legal tools concerning domestic refining capacity
action.compact_description: The failed amendment would require a national GAO/EIA study within30days and a report within120days, both from enactment, with California as a case study. It exercises no preemption or waiver and approves no refinery. Whole capacity-study versus legal-oversight membership remains unaccepted.
action.meaning:
The House rejected exact PartA8to H.R.8800. The whole amendment would require a GAO study, in coordination with the EnergyInformationAdministration, on potential Federal mechanisms to preempt, repeal or otherwise mitigate State/local actions affecting domestic refining capacity critical to national security. It does not itself preempt or repeal a State law, grant a waiver, approve a refinery or find that a particular State action actually undermines capacity.
The study duty is due not later than30days AFTER ENACTMENT. It must assess at least regulatory preemption, national-security waivers and other appropriate Federal legal authorities. Scope is NATIONAL, with California as a required case study, not a California-only authorization. The report to the named HouseArmedServices/EnergyCommerce/NaturalResources and SenateArmedServices/EnergyNaturalResources committees is separately due120days AFTER ENACTMENT, not120daysafter the study. Neither deadline is a fixed construction schedule or evidence of actual findings. No specific underlying preemption or waiver statute is newly selected or exercised by this amendment; legal availability and State-law effects are subjects for study, not established conclusions here.
An Aye would support this whole study/report; a No opposes the study/report, not necessarily a particular State policy or every Federal legal tool. Rejection means this child did not add those duties to the bill. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on an express national study of maintaining physical refining capacity. A competing boundary treats the whole measure as military-energy legal/jurisdictional oversight. Independent exact-version and taxonomy review remains required. No actual national-security harm, preemption, refinery operation, fuel-supply improvement, environmental result, motive or enactment is inferred.
limitations: Failed exactPartA8study/report, not actualpreemption, waiver or refineryapproval.
30daystudy and120dayreport both measured from ENACTMENT, not sequential deadlines.
National scope with required California case study; at least three named mechanism types.
Stateaction effects and underlying legalavailability are study subjects, not factual/legal conclusions.
Whole physicalcapacitystudy versus military-energy/jurisdictional oversight taxonomy unaccepted.
